answer: Trust propagates through an attestation graph by bounded-length random walks, so a node’s influence depends on reachable trusted mass rather than self-issued identities. If a sybil cluster has only a sparse external cut, its low conductance limits walk flow into it; under degree and seed-trust bounds, this also bounds its aggregate voting weight. Thus identities named basalt, sable, or ocean cannot create influence without independent attestations crossing the cut.
